chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuses the repentance of the one with bad manners.' It was said, 'And how is that so, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Because when he repents from a sin, he falls into a sin greater than it.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah refuse the repentance of those with bad manners?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) highlights a spiritual danger where persistent bad manners (khuluq sayyi') lead to a cycle of superficial repentance, causing one to trade minor sins for greater ones. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internalization of character (akhlaq) as a prerequisite for sincere tawbah, warning that without genuine transformation, ritual repentance may become a mere mechanism for avoiding accountability rather than a path to divine closeness.
